inventories.acceptance_criteria: Reject every new backend, Store, notify, daemon, webui/store, or webui/service import from production plural-handler files while allowing removals.
Add app and platform restrictions, owned expiring legacy paths, and bounded idempotent durable-cycle declarations before this analyzer accepts graph status approved.
Execute every declared build profile, attribute package-load/import-cycle failures to the exact profile, ratchet legacy handler imports, and default-deny undeclared module roots and edges.
Type-resolve and list every mutating fleet-db or repository call from HTTP and CLI adapters, with a per-file no-growth ratchet.
List every direct generic Lease and ActionLedger call site and assign its mechanism discriminator to a capability owner.
Record one aggregate owner and any coordinating owner for every product mutation selected for migration.

Record the accepted authority classes and mandatory wrong-workspace, unauthenticated, expired, and stale-fence tests for every selected migration command without claiming the Phase 2 tests already exist.
Declare the future atomic fleet-db command or recoverable process manager, idempotency key, retry behavior, and mandatory fault-injection tests for every selected cross-aggregate migration command.
Name every boot and long-lived component and record cadence, cancellation, readiness, retry, and owner.

Record reproducible startup, readiness, full-gate, runtime-loop, and frontend-chunk measurements; retain explicit nulls and procedures for pilot-only latency and round-trip metrics until Phase 2 makes them executable.
Check in the deterministic matrix and make target with explicit red rows, owners, setup commands, verification commands, and failure reporting.

decisions.rationale: Adopt the ten coarse capability owners and the documented Workspace versus Source Control and Artifacts boundaries.
Local operator mutations require a server-issued 256-bit credential stored in a mode-0600 runtime file; loopback location alone grants no authority.
A capability key is advertised only with Redis and Postgres parity for the active deployment; missing support fails readiness without fallback.
Workflow Catalog approve, unapprove, and activate is the first complete backend pilot after a behavior-neutral read seam.
Capability public roots live at internal/modules/<capability>; optional subpackages remain owner-private.
Compatibility facades expire after at most two migration waves unless an explicit reviewed owner and extension decision is recorded.

Mutating CLI commands discover an explicit configured management endpoint, never start a host implicitly, fail closed when unavailable, authenticate locally, and migrate family by family with output and exit-code compatibility.
